freezeOrder: Read and hash the three primary workflow sources; freeze these independent predicates before inspecting discovery candidates. Any subsequent narrower oracle is a retrospective, explicitly named partial facet, not a replacement for these predicates.

eslint-miner.goal: Deliver new high-signal, actionable behavioral ESLint rules addressing observed JavaScript/TypeScript failure patterns in actions/setup/js.
eslint-miner.acceptance: Distinct new enabled rules whose diagnostics independently agree with a source-defined behavioral defect on at least one real eligible target, reject matched nondefective controls, and supply an actionable repair; false-positive and false-negative acceptance beyond observed controls remains separate.
eslint-miner.partial: Independently verified before/after removal of a named behavioral defect from an existing eligible target linked to a delivered rule; never count rule declarations, fixtures, PRs, or agent success as defect removal.
eslint-miner.unit: distinct independently verified behavioral defect removals
eslint-miner.eligible: Existing JavaScript/TypeScript source files beneath actions/setup/js; implementations beneath eslint-factory.

eslint-refiner.goal: Improve existing ESLint factory rule precision, edge-case coverage, or actionable diagnostics using concrete diagnostic trends and feedback.
eslint-refiner.acceptance: Distinct existing-rule refinements with independently demonstrated incorrect-before/correct-after diagnostic behavior on a real reported case plus a matched control; issue creation and tests authored are not correctness.
eslint-refiner.partial: Independently verified resolution of a specific real false-positive, missed behavioral defect, or objectively incorrect diagnostic, followed through issue-to-implementation lineage. Native evidence must establish the claimed narrower improvement.
eslint-refiner.unit: distinct independently verified diagnostic defects resolved
eslint-refiner.eligible: Existing eslint-factory rules and their actions/setup/js targets; Go rule changes are excluded.

linter-miner.goal: Deliver specific, actionable, high-signal new Go analysis linters for recurring error-prone patterns not already covered by the existing linter set.
linter-miner.acceptance: Distinct new registered Go analyzers whose diagnostics independently agree with a behavioral defect on a real eligible Go target, reject matched nondefective controls, and identify an actionable repair.
linter-miner.partial: Independently verified before/after removal of a named Go behavioral defect from an existing eligible target linked to a delivered analyzer; implementation and registration alone do not establish useful diagnostic behavior.
linter-miner.unit: distinct independently verified Go behavioral defect removals
linter-miner.eligible: Non-test Go source beneath pkg and cmd; analyzer implementations beneath pkg/linters and registration in cmd/linters/main.go.

measurement.delivery: Assign a verified transition once to its immutable acceptance timestamp in start-inclusive, end-exclusive disjoint windows; a surviving snapshot is not new delivery.
measurement.unknowns: Missing native originals, incomplete eligible cohorts, unsupported source/executor eras and unverified semantics are null. Zero requires an exhausted eligible native cohort.
measurement.attribution: Repository outcome, corroborated output linkage, protected creation receipt and sole causal credit are separate. Editable markers are discovery only.
measurement.history: Prove source/compiled addition against the actual parent before asserting adoption. Missing Git objects are not absence or history exhaustion.
measurement.safeguards: Full rule correctness, precision/recall, regression safety and cost-effectiveness remain unmeasured unless separately demonstrated.
